ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, it is known that $\angle AOB = 80^\circ$, $OC$ is the bisector of $\angle AOB$, and $OD$ is the bisector of $\angle BOC$. What is the measure of $\angle AOD$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Given that $\angle AOB=80^\circ$ and OC is the bisector of $\angle AOB$, \\
it follows that $\angle AOC=\angle BOC=0.5\times 80^\circ=40^\circ$. \\
Also, since OD is the bisector of $\angle BOC$, \\
it follows that $\angle COD=\angle BOD=0.5\times 40^\circ=20^\circ$. \\
Therefore, $\angle AOD=\angle AOC+\angle COD=40^\circ+20^\circ=\boxed{60^\circ}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the attached figure, there are four rays all emitted from point O; the lowest is the horizontally rightward OB, upward in order are OD, OC, and the steepest at the top is OA; therefore C is located between A and B, D is located between C and B, and ∠AOD can be regarded as the sum of ∠AOC and ∠COD. From the order of the rays in the figure, ∠AOD = ∠AOC + ∠COD = 40° + 20° = 60°.
